k8s.title: Kubernetes
k8s.body: Day to day I work with Kubernetes, on EKS and GKE.

diagram.title: Diagram: a Kubernetes cluster's control plane, data plane and infra plane, provisioned with Terraform and Helm
diagram.desc: terraform apply creates the control plane (etcd, api-server, scheduler, controller), the data plane's two nodegroups on EKS or node pools on GKE, and the provider's add-ons. helm upgrade then installs the Helm charts. The control plane schedules pods onto the nodes until the cluster is ready. The diagram alternates between EKS and GKE.

cloud.title: Cloud & DevOps
cloud.body: I work on CI/CD pipelines in Azure DevOps and on infrastructure as code with Terraform, promoting releases across environments on AWS and GCP.

diagram.title: Diagram: an Azure DevOps pipeline promoting a release from dev to prod on EKS and GKE
diagram.desc: A git push runs terraform init, plan and apply, then helm upgrade, for the dev environment, and the release lands on AWS (EKS) and GCP (GKE). It is then promoted, and the same stages run for prod.

psegment.summary: Prostate cancer segmentation on MRI and CT scans with an ensemble of three U-Net models.
psegment.description:
This project aims to simplify and support prostate detection through a user-friendly frontend and a Python backend that handles convolutional neural network (CNN) processing. It is a Python backend and Vite.js frontend focused on automatic segmentation of prostate cancer regions in MRI and CT images.

The U-Net network was trained on two different datasets to obtain an ensemble of three models that work together to give the most accurate prediction despite dataset limitations. The work was inspired by the results of Recent Automatic Segmentation Algorithms of MRI Prostate Regions: A Review.

deepl.summary: A Gradio workflow that degrades MusicGen outputs and restores them with Demucs, S-NMF and a custom U-Net.
deepl.description:
Audio Restoration Studio is a Gradio workflow that stress-tests generative audio models by degrading MusicGen outputs and restoring them with Demucs, S-NMF and a custom U-Net trained on curated datasets.

The toolkit compares spectrograms, quality metrics and checkpoints, so we could study denoising strategies for deep learning pipelines.

angel.summary: A Chrome extension with a CNN-powered Flask backend that rates the safety of URLs as you browse.
angel.description:
Angel analyses URL requests during navigation and evaluates the security of a website from the predictions of a convolutional neural network. It is built as a Chrome extension and a Flask server.

The extension intercepts the requests made by the browser and sends them to the server, which runs a model we trained on a modified dataset. The prediction goes back to the extension, which shows the result to the user.

ml.summary: Neural forward kinematics for 2–5 DOF robot arms, and image classification of racing-car actions in OpenAI Gym.
ml.description: The two homeworks of the Machine Learning course. The descriptions below are quoted from my written reports.

firsthw.title: Homework 1: forward kinematics
firsthw.body: The primary objective is to develop and train neural network models that learn the forward kinematics (FK) of robotic manipulators with 2, 3 and 5 degrees of freedom. Forward kinematics determines the position and orientation of a robot's end-effector from its joint angles; the networks approximate the FK function accurately enough to predict end-effector states for arbitrary joint configurations.

secondhw.title: Homework 2: image classification
secondhw.body: The goal is to classify the behaviour of a racing car in the OpenAI Gym environment: 96×96 colour images, each corresponding to one of the five actions available to control the car.

iot.summary: A ROS and Gazebo simulation where balloons cache sensor data to answer a base station's requests.
iot.description:
An IoT configuration and simulation problem: build a suitable environment with Gazebo and ROS (driven from Python) to meet the project brief.

Balloons are always connected to the base station and are deployed so that together they guarantee radio coverage for every mobile sensor. Each balloon has limited storage, which it uses to provide a proxy caching service to the base station. Since the balloons cannot store everything the sensors produce, they must choose which data to keep in order to satisfy the base station's application-specific requests.

cipensaele.summary: Scheduling and reservation system with a React frontend and a Node.js and Express backend.
cipensaele.description:
A web-based calendar and scheduling system with a React frontend and a Node.js backend. The frontend renders a calendar view and handles appointments, reservations and reports, talking to the backend over HTTP.

The backend owns the business logic and data: it exposes APIs to create, update and delete calendar events, manages authentication and authorisation, and stores data securely in a database.

Caching reduces server requests and speeds up data retrieval, and encryption protects sensitive data to keep it confidential and intact.

fourever.summary: An Ethereum DApp to create, trade and earn NFTs through an in-game quest system.
fourever.description:
A DApp that lets users and companies manage their own NFTs. It runs on Ethereum and uses smart contracts to handle the creation, ownership and transfer of NFTs.

Players get a clear interface to manage their NFTs, a marketplace to buy and sell them, and a quest system that rewards completed tasks and challenges, all in the context of an online game.

hciw.summary: A React Native app paired with an ESP32 sensor that counts reps and flags posture issues in real time.
hciw.description:
Gym Tracker is a cross-platform companion built with React Native for the Human–Computer Interaction on the Web course. It pairs with an ESP32-powered sensor to count repetitions, check posture and highlight form issues in real time.

The project also ships Arduino firmware and Python tooling to stream, label and visualise workouts, so athletes can review their sessions from any device.

dohr.summary: A web companion for a role-playing video game, where players share lore and manage their inventory. My B.Sc. thesis.
dohr.description:
A website that acts as an online interface for the video game: a virtual space where players exchange information about the game world and manage their inventory.

The interface is designed to be simple and intuitive while staying visually consistent with the game's theme.
